newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end slightly off on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end slightly off on consolidation.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended slightly lower on Wednesday after hitting another record high for the third time this week as the market went through a consolidation phase, brokers said.
"The index eased slightly at the closing, but strong gains in blue chips Sampoerna and Indocement and also active buying in Surya Semesta kept the index from a steeper fall," a local broker said.
"It's a pretty good correction. After the index gained steadily in the last few days, this indicates it will be corrected steadily too," he said.
Brokers said the market was not affected by the turmoil in the baht after Thai authorities announced a managed float of the currency earlier in the day.
"I didn't see any direct impact of the Thai baht on the Jakarta stock market today," Naotaka Ikeda, director of Asian Development Securities (ADS) brokerage, said.
The Jakarta Composite Index eased 1.46 points, or 0.20 percent, to 730.16 points after hitting a record high of 734.02 points early in the day .
Losers led gainers by 81 to 54, with 68 counters unchanged. Total turnover was about 654 billion rupiah.
Another local broker predicted the market would continue consolidating on Thursday after its steep rise in the last few days.
"Trading will be a little bit slow tomorrow, I guess, unless some companies announce fresh corporate action," a broker with Vickers Ballas Tamara said.
Profit-taking was seen in blue chips Semen Gresik, Telkom and Citra Marga after recent sharp gains, brokers said.
Speculation over possible private placements had boosted sentiment towards secondaries Surya Semesta and Eterindo Wahana, brokers said.
Property firm Surya Semesta was the most active stock with around 79 million shares traded. It closed up 50 rupiah at 1,325 after touching a high of 1,400 rupiah.
The company's investor relations officer Percy Marimba declined to comment on the rumours.

But he said Surya Semesta was in the final stage of negotiations with foreign firms on two projects -- a container port at its industrial estate in Karawang, West Java, and the setting up a construction company. He declined to give further details.
